jobs.description:
**Position Description**
------------------------

**Open until filled**  

**Priority Screening:****Thursday, August 27, 2026****Exam:** **26/41C14/08GM** **Associate Water Resources Hydrologist**
$9,332 – $12,746 Monthly  

The County of Monterey is committed to honoring the service and sacrifice of veterans and eligible military spouses and awards veterans’ preference points for this recruitment. To learn more about the eligibility requirements and the process, be sure to read the **Hiring Preference for Veterans and Eligible Military Spouses** section located towards the end of this job flier.


The Monterey County Water Resources Agency (MCWRA or Agency) is an independent, special purpose public agency staffed with dedicated employees and focused on water resources management in Monterey County. The Agency was created via a California Water Code Appendix in a statute known as the Monterey County Water Resources Agency Act. The Agency is governed by the Monterey County Water Resources Agency Board of Supervisors for larger policy matters and a nine\-member Board of Directors for more in\-depth oversight.


The Agency provides the following services: control of flood and storm waters, flood warning and monitoring, water conservation, protection of water quality, reclamation of water and the exchange of water. Fundamental to the Agency’s mission to sustainably manage water resources while minimizing impacts from flooding, the MCWRA owns and operates the Nacimiento and San Antonio reservoirs and dams, a hydroelectric facility at Nacimiento Reservoir, the Salinas River Diversion Facility, the Castroville Seawater Intrusion Project, the Salinas Valley Reclamation Project, various drainage facilities, and numerous wells.


MCWRA executes long\-term groundwater and surface water monitoring programs throughout the Salinas Valley Groundwater Basin and provides technical expertise on water resource management and planning throughout Monterey County.

**The Position:**  

 MCWRA seeks qualified candidates to fill two Associate Water Resources Hydrologist vacancies: one in the Operations section and one in the Hydrology and Environmental Resources section.


This position is responsible for supervising assigned program functional activities and professional and technical level personnel. The candidate must perform a variety of complex hydrologic and hydrogeologic assignments and projects that include overseeing aspects of the operations and evaluation of the reservoir release program, flood warning system and other programs related to MCWRA facilities, and the groundwater monitoring program.


The ideal candidates will demonstrate integrity; flexibility and adaptability; be able to navigate complex situations with professionalism and poise; be able to communicate technical and policy information effectively to diverse audiences; and be organized and efficient to complete multiple projects concurrently. This candidate must be able to work collaboratively in a dynamic environment, seek multi\-benefit solutions for new and ongoing projects or programs, and demonstrate good independent judgment.


The ideal candidate for the position in the Operations Section will have a strong background in the operation of water resource\-related facilities such as dams, reservoirs, water diversion structures, or flood conveyance systems; flood warning systems; water rights compliance and reporting; and project and grant management.


The ideal candidate for the position in the Hydrology and Environmental Resources section will have a strong background in groundwater and surface water data collection methodologies, equipment, and industry best practices; data management and monitoring network evaluation; and analysis and reporting of complex datasets.

*The Eligible List established by this recruitment may be used to fill current and future vacancies on a regular full\-time, part\-time, or temporary basis County\-wide.*


**Examples of Duties**
----------------------


**Examples of duties:*** Supervises and participates in the work of professional hydrology staff responsible for the planning, design, development, operation and maintenance of the department or agency capital improvement projects and programs including flood control, surface and groundwater quality and water supply, storage, treatment and distribution facilities and systems; ensures work quality and adherence to professional codes, standards and department or agency specifications; may provide supervision over assigned maintenance or operations functions.
* Counsels employees, appraises performance, prepares documentation, recommends merit increases, and issues discipline; provides for or participates in employee training and development; conducts interviews and recommends selection of candidates; coaches and mentors subordinate staff.
* Performs the more complex, difficult and large scale hydrologic and hydrogeologic planning, specification, feasibility analysis and calculations for water resources related projects and programs; functions as an expert in assigned area of expertise; prepares conceptual designs and supervises detail design of project phases by other staff and engineers.
* Reviews and evaluates groundwater and surface water supply, availability and/or quality, as well as trends over time; maintains water quality assurance documentation; supervises the operation/evaluation of the Agency’s reservoirs including the conservation release program.
* Oversees the operation and maintenance of water quality, hydrologic, hydrogeologic, land use, well, or groundwater extraction reporting data base; graphs and charts data; prepares maps and reports based on data analysis. presentations

jobs.title: Contract/ Part-time Program Coordinator - Arts Instructor (Pacific View Arts Center)
jobs.description:
**The Position**
----------------

  

  

The City of Encinitas is seeking creative and dedicated Program Coordinator \- Arts Instructors to support engaging arts programming at the Pacific View Arts Center. Program Coordinator \- Arts Instructors develop and deliver lessons across diverse disciplines—such as visual, performing, and multimedia arts—to help participants learn subject matter and skills that will contribute to educational development, promote creative expression, and encourage social engagement. This role is ideal for experienced educators who excel at designing curriculum, leading dynamic classes, and creating welcoming spaces where participants of all ages can explore and grow. Program Coordinator \- Arts instructors report to the Assistant Center Manager.  

***Program Coordinator \- Arts Instructor is a part\-time, temporary position. Incumbents work less than 999 hours a year. Work schedules may vary and incumbents may be required to work weekends and evenings.***
**Examples of Important \& Essential Duties (included but not limited to)**
---------------------------------------------------------------------------


Examples of Important \& Essential Duties (included but not limited to):

* Develop class ideas, create lesson plans and establish goals for a variety of arts programs such as drawing, painting, mosaic, collage, fiber art, printmaking, photography, dance, music, graphic design, animation and commercial art etc.
* Instruct participants of all ages in group settings of up to 16\-32 participants at various ability levels in arts classes, workshops, and youth camps.
* Provide appropriate instruction and activities for participants to meet objectives and enjoy the creative process. Lead classes through engaging teaching techniques that demonstrate clarity and creativity with encouragement for participants to reach their personal goals.
* Coordinate with volunteers to assist with programs.
* Select and requisition instructional materials; maintain inventory records.
* Ensure that all spaces and classes are safe, welcoming, and inclusive to all participants.


Essential Job Functions

* Resolves unusual or difficult customer service requirements without the necessity of referral to program managers.
* Performs a full range of duties, which require the application of comprehensive and specialized knowledge regarding arts education and classroom management.
* Coordinates, plans, implements, and assists in the management of arts education programs in the absence of direct supervision.
* Instructs others from outside the department and program in the methods and requirements to accomplish Pacific View Arts Center arts education priorities.
* Operates with considerable independence in maintenance of assignments and special projects related to assigned area of responsibility and or arts discipline.
* Possesses expertise in an arts discipline that is offered as a regular class course at the Pacific View Arts Center.
* Must be able to manage art supplies, equipment, tools and classroom, and storage spaces. Must be able to exert a negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to lift, carry, push, pull, or otherwise move objects.
* Requires the ability to read and interpret a variety of correspondence, reports, handbooks, forms, and lists, and to prepare correspondence, basic reports, forms, and instructional materials following prescribed formats.
* Requires the ability to conceptualize and create art form(s) and encourage creative flow while applying artistic principles.
* Performs other related work as required.

**Minimum Qualifications**
--------------------------


**Training and Experience** (position requirements at entry):
High School Diploma, or General Equivalency Diploma (G.E.D.), and at least two years of responsible arts instructor experience including at least one year of teaching in classrooms, or an equivalent combination of education and experience sufficient to successfully perform the essential duties of the job such as those listed above.  

  

A Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) degree from an accredited college or university is highly desirable.  


**Application Process and Deadline**
------------------------------------


A complete **application** with an attached **resume** is required. *\*\*\* Incomplete application packets will not be reviewed \*\*\**  

  

**This job posting is open until the position is filled. Applications will be reviewed periodically, and q****ualified applicants will be invited for interviews via email.**

Please note that all applications must be submitted online through this portal in order to be considered.***

jobs.description:
**Job Details**
---------------

  

  

  

**EXTRA HELP – TEMPORARY WORK ASSIGNMENT**


An individual may be hired as Extra Help Employee for a temporary work assignment at such compensation as determined by County of Lake personnel rules and regulations.

* Extra Help Employees are typically hired at an hourly rate of pay at the first step of the salary range.
* Extra Help Employees are paid only for hours worked.
* Extra Help Employees are entitled to legally mandated benefits, which does not include paid vacation or holidays.
* Extra Help Employees do not have status.
* Extra Help Employment is temporary and may end at any time.

 **EXTRA\-HELP APPOINTMENT** \- Extra help positions are limited to no more than 25 hours per week (unless position is considered seasonal) and no more than 900 hours per fiscal year, whether upon certification from an eligible list or upon authorization to appoint any person who meets the minimum qualifications of the classification.**\*\*SEASONAL EMPLOYEE:**
An extra help employee who works a seasonal job (tied to an actual season, not just part\-year) for a portion of the year and who will not perform any work for the County for at least 26 consecutive weeks between seasons definition is subject to future change as terminology is further defined by the ACA.* Employees must be terminated for the 26 weeks that they are not performing any work.
* This position will be working 40 hours/week from April \- October each year

**CalPERS RETIREE:** Public Employees’ Retirement Law (PERL). Effective January 1, 2012, Assembly Bill (AB) 1028 amended Government Code (G.C.) sections 21224, 21229, and 21221(h) concerning employment after retirement. If an individual is receiving a CalPERS retirement benefit, the eligibility to work an Extra Help – Temporary Work Assignment may be restricted to only temporary assignments for a special project or backlog of work.

 Possession of, or ability to obtain, an appropriate valid California driver's license.**Education and Experience:**

Experience with Geographic Information Systems (GIS) is preferred.
Additional directly related experience and/or education may be substituted.

**SUMMARY OF JOB DESCRIPTION:**  

CAPE is seeking a field\-oriented Project Scientist to support environmental remediation projects nationwide. This mid\-level role combines hands\-on fieldwork, GIS and geospatial data management, environmental data evaluation, and technical writing. The successful candidate will be comfortable working at active project sites, coordinating with subcontractors and field crews, and producing clear, defensible technical plans and reports. Candidates with direct remediation experience \- including remedial action, system operation, soil excavation, groundwater treatment, or similar implementation work \- are strongly preferred over candidates whose experience is limited to site investigation.
  
  

Lead and support field activities for environmental remediation projects, including soil, groundwater, surface water, sediment, and air sampling; drilling oversight; lithologic logging; monitoring well installation or abandonment; and remedial system operation and monitoring.
  
Work safely and effectively on active construction and remediation sites, including coordination with subcontractors, drillers, equipment operators, trades, and project field teams.
  
Use GIS, GPS, and related geospatial tools to collect, manage, analyze, and present field data. Develop maps, figures, and spatial products using ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Field Maps, Trimble or comparable platforms.
  
Prepare and review high\-quality technical documents such as work plans, sampling and analysis plans, quality assurance or quality control plans, field reports, remedial action reports, construction completion reports, regulatory submittals, and proposal content.
  
Evaluate environmental and laboratory data; prepare tables, graphs, figures, and statistical summaries; and communicate findings and recommendations to project teams and clients.
  
Support remedial design and planning, field implementation, quality control, project scheduling, cost estimating, and subcontractor management.
  
Interpret field conditions and project data, identify issues, and make timely recommendations with support from senior technical staff as needed.
  
Collaborate with project managers, engineers, scientists, and geologists to meet client requirements, budgets, schedules, and CAPE technical quality standards.
  
Mentor junior staff and contribute to the continued development of field procedures, data\-management practices, and technical deliverables.
  
  

**SALARY:**  

$75,000 \-$105,000 annually, commensurate with experience and qualifications.
  
  

**TRAVEL:**  

Up to 50% on an annual basis
  
  

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:**  

Bachelor's degree in geology, hydrogeology, environmental science, engineering, or a closely related field.
  
Approximately 3\-8 years of relevant professional experience in environmental consulting, remediation, geoscience, or a related field.
  
Demonstrated willingness and ability to spend significant time in the field, work outdoors in varying conditions, support early starts or extended field days, and travel approximately 50% depending on project needs.
  
Hands\-on experience supporting environmental field programs, including work around drilling operations, excavations, heavy equipment, sampling activities, or remediation systems.
  
Practical GIS experience, including ArcGIS Pro and/or ArcGIS Field Maps, and experience with GPS data collection, processing, mapping, or geospatial data management.
  
Strong technical writing skills, with demonstrated experience preparing clear, organized, and defensible environmental plans, reports, field documentation, or regulatory deliverables.
  
Strong analytical, organizational, interpersonal, and verbal communication skills; ability to manage multiple assignments and meet deadlines with attention to detail.
  
Valid U.S. driver’s license and ability to satisfy project\-specific background, badging, medical, and physical requirements.
  
  

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
  
  

Direct environmental remediation experience, particularly remedial action implementation, soil or groundwater treatment, remediation system operation and maintenance, excavation oversight, or construction quality control. Experience limited primarily to investigation or assessment is less preferred.
  
Experience supporting federal environmental projects for USACE, NAVFAC, AFCEC, EPA, or other Department of Defense agencies.
  
Knowledge of CERCLA, RCRA, federal and state environmental regulations, and environmental quality assurance/quality control requirements.
  
Experience with Trimble Business Center, AutoCAD, Surfer, EnviroData, Adobe Illustrator, statistical software, or environmental modeling tools.
  
Professional certification or progress toward certification, such as GIT, PG, EIT, PE, or GISP.
  
Current Construction Quality Management for Contractors (CQM\-C) certification issued through USACE or NAVFAC.
  
Current 40\-hour HAZWOPER training and annual refresher; additional safety, first aid/CPR, or hazardous materials training is beneficial.
  
Master’s degree in geology, hydrogeology, environmental science, engineering, or a related field.

jobs.title: Junior Utility Project Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Gaucher \& Associates, Inc.** 

**Junior Project Coordinator**

For the past 29 years, Gaucher \& Associates, Inc. has been relied upon to manage the installation and activation of utility services to provide solutions that meet our clients’ utility concerns. We are experts at utility project management, focusing on electricity, natural gas, water, sewer, data and voice services for commercial clients. We have created long term relationships with clients, utility companies, and contractors and have opened, ON TIME, over 10,000 locations in all 50 states and 29 countries. We deliver excellence to diverse companies, from Fortune 10 to start\-ups, and we believe we can help any team manage their utility concerns and achieve their goals.

**WHO WE ARE**

**Our Mission**

We are experts in utility project management. We deliver consistent results through research and coordination to eliminate our client’s utility concerns.

**Our Vision**

As a trusted leader, we recognize the impact of utilities on global sustainability and the importance of human\-to\-human connections. We are committed to innovative solutions that encourage our client’s economic growth, environmental responsibility, and social awareness.

**Our Values**

1\. Practice compassion for ourselves and others

2\. Commit to unwavering reliability

3\. Champion integrity in all we do

4\. Deliver excellence

5\. Value knowledge: stay curious, respect wisdom

6\. Build and sustain collaborative relationships

Role Overview

The Junior Research Associate will support Gaucher’s Utility Due Diligence and Project Management efforts by performing research, setting up new projects in internal systems, and assisting with client deliverables. This role will help ensure accurate, timely reporting on utility availability, fees, and timelines, and provide essential administrative and project support to keep client projects on schedule.

Qualifications

· Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Business Administration, Environmental Science, or a related field preferred.

· Minimum 2 years of related experience in construction, utility work, project coordination, or project management required.

· Familiarity with project management workflows.

· Ability to conduct professional correspondence and document research findings clearly.

· Understanding of utility processes (electric, gas, water, sewer) is a plus.

· Strong organizational and time management skills with the ability to handle multiple projects simultaneously.

· Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to present findings effectively.

· Detail\-oriented with a commitment to accuracy and quality.

· Comfortable working independently and in a collaborative team environment.

Skills

· Research and data analysis

· Project setup and milestone tracking

· Vendor and client communication

· Document preparation and reporting

· Problem\-solving and troubleshooting (especially with billing or utility questions)

· Database management and information entry

· Adaptability to changing project needs and deadlines

**Key Responsibilities**

· Assist with Utility Due Diligence Reports (UDDRs), including researching processes, timelines, and costs for utility connections and upgrades.

· Conduct web research and communicate with utility providers, municipalities, engineers, architects, and clients to gather relevant data.

· Support creation of UDDR documents and entry of research findings into the proprietary database.

· Verify and update vendor information; create new vendor records as needed.

· Track and communicate changes in utility company rates, rules, and policies to internal teams and clients.

· Provide ongoing specialized research for client requests, including sustainable and emissions\-reduction utility options.

· Set up all new facilities in the internal database, ensuring accurate entry of client, project, and vendor information.

· Establish and maintain project milestones within the project management system to support timely delivery.

· Populate UDDR forms in Tririga, including vendor status, project status, and other assigned fields.

· Update project timelines and monitor project status throughout the UDDR cycle.

· Investigate and resolve billing inquiries for newly opened sites.

· Coordinate and order site visits with plumbers, sewer scope vendors, or other contractors; track timing and gather results.

· Liaise with vendors and stakeholders to ensure accurate data collection and reporting.

· Participate in client and Gaucher team meetings, effectively communicating research findings and supporting project discussions.

· Answer stakeholder questions and provide clarification on reports and findings.

· Act as a point of contact for UPM for application submissions and data collection for project support.

· Attend weekly one\-on\-one meetings with supervisor and internal team check\-ins.

· Perform additional research and administrative duties as assigned.

· Contribute to the continuous improvement of research workflows, vendor resources, and reporting accuracy.
